title: API 580 Training in New Orleans: RBI Exam Prep Online
description: API 580 exam prep for RBI planners, engineers and inspectors at the Garyville, Norco, Chalmette and Meraux refineries and river terminals. Self-paced online.
h1: API 580 Risk Based Inspection Exam Prep for Lower Mississippi Refineries, Plants and Terminals
html:
API 580 exam prep for risk-based inspection teams on the lower river

Risk-based inspection is how most large sites between LaPlace and Chalmette decide where their inspection effort goes: which vessels open at the next turnaround, which piping circuits get more CMLs, which tanks can safely run longer. The API 580 certification shows that a person understands the method behind those decisions. This page is for inspection planners, reliability and corrosion engineers, unit inspectors and process safety staff in and around New Orleans who are preparing for the API 580 examination.

There is no Atlantis classroom in New Orleans. The API 580 course is online and self-paced, and an instructor answers questions as you work, which suits engineers whose diaries fill up around turnarounds. The American Petroleum Institute sets the eligibility rules, administers the API 580 examination and certifies those who pass; the course is preparation for that examination, and Atlantis has no API approval or accreditation as a training provider.

The people who sit API 580 between LaPlace and Chalmette

  • Inspection planners and RBI coordinators who run the site's RBI software and turn its output into inspection plans for each turnaround.
  • Corrosion and materials engineers who write the damage mechanism reviews behind every corrosion loop.
  • Certified API 510, 570 and 653 inspectors who sit on the RBI team and want the method formally behind their judgement.
  • Reliability and process safety engineers who need to defend inspection frequencies in audits.
  • Terminal and pipeline integrity staff applying risk methods to tank fields and dock systems.

Eligibility is simpler than for the inspector programmes: anyone already holding a current API 510, 570 or 653 certificate is eligible without further proof. Everyone else qualifies on education plus petrochemical industry experience within the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree or higher, two years with a two-year degree, three with a high school diploma and five or more with no formal education. A chemical engineer two years into an inspection or reliability role at a Hahnville or Norco plant is often already eligible.

Why lower-river sites lean on RBI

Scale is part of it. EIA's 2026 refinery capacity survey lists about 1.38 million barrels per calendar day of crude capacity at five refineries on this stretch: Marathon at Garyville, Shell and Valero at Norco, Chalmette Refining at Chalmette and Valero at Meraux. Add Dow's St. Charles Operations, a 2,000-acre integrated petrochemical complex at Hahnville, the renewable diesel plant at Norco and more than 40 liquid and dry bulk terminals along the Port of South Louisiana's 54 miles of river, and the list of inspectable items becomes very long indeed. Time-based intervals applied to all of it would spend effort evenly where risk is anything but even.

The rules leave room for that choice. OSHA's process safety management standard expects inspection and testing to follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, and frequencies to be consistent with manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practice, more often where operating experience says so. API 510, API 570 and API 653 allow risk-based inspection as a way of setting intervals, with conditions. An RBI assessment, done to API RP 580 and documented, is the evidence an owner shows when asked why a vessel is opened every six years and its neighbour every ten. The guide to PSM, RAGAGEP and the API codes and the comparison of time-based and risk-based intervals cover the background.

Five refineries, five risk pictures

The same method gives very different rankings on neighbouring sites, because the units differ. EIA's figures and the owners' own descriptions suggest where the high-ranked items tend to cluster:

RefineryWhat EIA and the owner listWhere probability of failure tends to concentrate
Marathon, Garyville617,000 b/cd crude; 130,000 b/sd hydrocracking; 140,000 b/sd low-pressure reforming; 110,500 b/sd delayed cokingHydroprocessing reactors and effluent trains, coker drums and heater outlets, reformer hydrogen service
Shell, Norco231,153 b/cd crude; 118,800 b/sd catalytic cracking; 44,000 b/sd hydrocracking; site dating from 1929FCC reactor, regenerator and slurry systems, older equipment with long inspection histories
Valero St. Charles, Norco215,000 b/cd crude; 86,000 b/sd coking; 113,000 b/sd hydrocracking; alkylation expansion announced in 2019Coker and hydrocracker circuits, acid service in alkylation
Chalmette Refining (PBF)190,000 b/cd crude; dual-train coking; light and heavy crude; specialty chemicalsCrude and vacuum units exposed to changing crude quality, coker trains
Valero, Meraux125,000 b/cd crude; 48,700 b/sd hydrocracking; 22,000 b/sd solvent deasphalting; no coker or catalytic cracker listedHydrocracker high-pressure loop, deasphalting solvent circuits

The right-hand column is a starting assumption, not a result; each site's own damage mechanism review and inspection data decide the ranking. Consequence also varies more than candidates expect. A release on a river refinery may involve occupied buildings, neighbouring communities, the levee, the dock and the shipping channel, and how quickly a unit can be isolated changes the outcome as much as the size of the hole. API 580 asks you to think about both sides of the risk equation before reaching for an inspection.

Crude slates, storms and other reassessment triggers

An RBI assessment describes a plant at a moment, and the lower river gives that moment a short shelf life. Crude reaches these refineries by ship, by barge, through LOOP's offshore port and by pipeline from the St. James hub, so the slate can change faster than at a landlocked site; PBF says Chalmette is capable of processing both light and heavy crude. Sulfur, acid number, chloride and solids feed straight into the probability of failure assigned to crude units and everything downstream, so a sustained change in feed is a reason to revisit the assessment.

Other common triggers: a management-of-change that alters temperature, pressure or chemistry; an inspection that finds a damage rate the model did not predict; an excursion outside an integrity operating window; a new unit or a new feed, such as renewable feedstocks; and a storm, a high-water event on the river or an extended outage that leaves insulation soaked and equipment idle. The codes that let RBI set intervals also expect the assessment to be reviewed periodically and when such changes occur, and the owner's procedure should name the triggers. On the exam, expect scenarios that ask what should prompt a reassessment, and which data should be gathered first.

Worked closed-book reasoning: comparing two items by area risk

API 580 is closed-book, and its questions test reasoning rather than formulas. One classic idea is that risk combines probability and consequence, so an item with a low probability can still outrank one with a high probability. Suppose a team expresses consequence as an affected area:

  • Item A, a hot high-pressure separator outlet line: probability of failure 1 in 10,000 per year (0.0001), consequence area 20,000 sq ft. Risk = 0.0001 × 20,000 = 2.0 sq ft per year.
  • Item B, a light-ends drum: probability of failure 1 in 1,000 per year (0.001), consequence area 1,500 sq ft. Risk = 0.001 × 1,500 = 1.5 sq ft per year.

Item A ranks higher despite a tenfold lower probability. Now ask what inspection can do. If Item B's dominant mechanism is general thinning and an effective thickness survey cuts its probability by a factor of five, its risk falls to 0.3 sq ft per year. If Item A's dominant concern is a cracking or hydrogen-attack mechanism that spot thickness readings cannot detect, more thickness readings change nothing; only a technique suited to the mechanism, or a consequence measure such as faster isolation, reduces its risk. The numbers are illustrative; what the exam rewards is recognising that inspection reduces risk only through the probability side, and only when the method can find the damage.

Inspection effectiveness and the data a river-plant model runs on

RBI is only as good as its inputs, and on old, much-modified units the inputs are scattered. A model needs design and construction data, the corrosion loops and their damage mechanisms from an API RP 571 review, thickness history from the CML programme, process conditions from the plant historian, and the integrity operating windows that keep those conditions within limits; API RP 584 covers the windows, and the API 584 explainer and API 571 explainer summarise both documents.

Past inspections count only as far as they were capable of finding the damage. API RP 581, the quantitative method, grades inspection effectiveness in categories from highly effective down to ineffective, and RP 580 discusses effectiveness qualitatively; either way, a visual check of an insulated line is not credited like an insulation-off survey, and a spot thickness reading earns no credit at all against a cracking mechanism. Data gaps should be recorded as such, because an assumed value quietly hides risk.

Terminals, renewable fuel and LNG: RBI beyond the refinery fence

The method travels. IMTT's St. Rose terminal lists 14.7 million barrels of storage in 203 tanks, and for-hire terminals of that kind can use RBI under API 653 to set tank inspection intervals, provided the assessment meets the code's conditions and no pipeline breakout tank rule says otherwise. Renewable diesel units need their own damage mechanism review, because the feed is not crude. Venture Global's Plaquemines LNG, in commercial operation for its first phase from 2026, raises consequence questions about cryogenic releases that refinery models were not built for. API 580 itself stays generic: it tests the principles that apply to all of these, not the details of any one industry.

Studying API 580 next to planning and turnaround work

The examination has 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 of them scored and 10 unscored pretest items, answered closed-book in 3.25 hours against a set passing scaled score. It draws on the API 580 Body of Knowledge, which is built on API RP 580, so read the Body of Knowledge for your window before planning anything else.

Planners and engineers tend to be busiest exactly when an exam window approaches turnaround season, so pick a window that leaves room. A workable sequence: the vocabulary and structure of RP 580 first (risk, probability, consequence, risk targets, the RBI team, documentation), then damage mechanisms and inspection effectiveness, then the management of an RBI programme over time, finishing with timed closed-book papers. Write your own short definitions of each term, test them against the RP 580 text, and send the instructor any distinction that will not settle, such as the difference between a risk driver and a consequence of failure. You take the exam at a test centre, or by remote proctoring where API offers it; Prometric lists test centres in and around New Orleans. Recertification follows a three-year term; you can apply from 90 days before expiry, with a 90-day grace period, and API does not currently ask for employment verification to recertify.

Exam preparation is not an RBI study

Passing API 580 shows you understand the method; it does not produce an assessment for your site. When an owner needs the study itself, Atlantis runs remote RBI studies from the site's data and inspection history, separately from this course, and the owner's inspector of record approves the resulting intervals. Fitness-for-service assessment is a different discipline under a different standard and is not part of either the course or that work. The API 580 course page describes the curriculum, and enquiries from employers sponsoring several candidates are welcome, with fees quoted on request.

faq.q: Must I hold API 510, 570 or 653 to sit API 580 in New Orleans?
faq.a: No. If you already hold one of those three certifications and it is current, API treats you as eligible, but none of them is a prerequisite. Without one, API accepts education plus petrochemical industry experience within the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree, three with a high school diploma, or five or more with no formal education.

faq.q: Does work at a river terminal count as petrochemical industry experience?
faq.a: Often it can, since terminals on the lower Mississippi store and move crude, refined products and chemicals. API judges each application on what you describe and what your employer confirms, so set out the facilities, the products and your duties plainly. If you are unsure, the education-plus-experience table on the API 580 page is the place to check before you apply.

faq.q: Our site uses semi-quantitative RBI. Does the exam assume a fully quantitative method?
faq.a: No. API RP 580 deliberately covers qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches as points on one spectrum, and the examination tests the shared principles: risk, probability and consequence of failure, inspection planning, data quality and reassessment. API RP 581 is the published quantitative method, and some sites use it, but a semi-quantitative programme is equally within the scope of RP 580.

faq.q: After a hurricane, does our RBI assessment have to be redone?
faq.a: Not automatically from scratch, but a major storm is a classic reason to revisit it. Wet insulation, flooded foundations, damaged floating roofs and equipment left depressurised or unheated through an outage can all change damage rates or reveal new damage. A good procedure lists storms and high water as triggers and says which checks come first before intervals are relied on again.

faq.q: Will passing API 580 make me the RBI lead at a Norco or Garyville refinery?
faq.a: Certification shows you understand the method; the employer decides who leads the programme, usually on experience with the site's units, software and data. Holding API 510 or 570 as well helps, because the plans an RBI lead writes are carried out under those codes.

faq.q: Can I sit API 580 without travelling to a test centre?
faq.a: API 580 is taken at a test centre or, where API offers it, by remote proctoring; check the current arrangements on API's programme page when you apply. If you sit at a centre, Prometric lists locations in and around New Orleans, and you book after API accepts your application.

faq.q: Is API 580 useful for a process engineer at a Hahnville chemical plant?
faq.a: Yes, if your work touches inspection planning, management of change or process safety. RBI depends on process data and on knowing how conditions drive damage, which is a process engineer's territory. The certification helps you speak the inspection group's language when you review an assessment or set an integrity operating window.
